page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong performance. However, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth present notable tradeoffs. Multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category, while memory bandwidth read-only tests, both small and large blocks, rank in the bottom 25%. Additionally, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are weak, placing in the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r8a.xlarge offers a high density of dedicated memory resources relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive local storage or high-throughput database operations. Given the strong single-core capabilities but weaker multi-threaded scaling and read memory bandwidth, this instance is suited for memory-intensive applications, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without heavy parallel database demands.
